articleTitle: Strategies to finance your higher education: Strategies include cost reduction and academic planning, but the most important involves identifying, evaluating, and selecting financial aid
abstract: Students can employ many strategies to finance their higher education, including cost reduction, academic planning, and direct financial aid. We will not discuss cost reduction here, for it is subject enough for a separate article. It is sufficient to state that cost-reduction decisions often have farreaching implications, and the choices students make in this area reflect personal lifestyle and sacrifice. We will, however, address specific strategies in the areas of academic planning and direct student aid. Using strategies in both these areas will enhance any college student's pursuit of higher education.

articleTitle: The new Hewlett-Packard Interface Loop: The new Hewlett-Packard Interface Loop (HP-IL) is a bit-serial interface for battery-operable systems with controllers, like the HP-41
abstract: Hewlett-Packard has introduced a new bit-serial interface that makes it possible for hand-held computers, such as the HP-41, to control instruments and peripherals. The interface, called the HP-IL for Hewlett-Packard Interface Loop, uses a two-wire cable that leads from the output port of one device to the input port of the next, until all devices form a closed loop. The loop is unidirectional with commands and data moving around the loop at rates up to five kilobytes per second. The new interface enables hand-held computers to control and read data from a new HP digital multimeter and to interact with a new digital tape cassette drive and a new thermal printer/plotter.

articleTitle: Successful career planning: You are in charge: You can't design your future, but the decisions that shape your career are made by you. You are the pathfinder
abstract: A career is the summation of our experiences — in life, in school, and in various jobs. If we plan our careers, i.e., maintain some control over decisions to be made in these areas, our chances for a “successful” career are enhanced. Furthermore, the sooner we start on career planning, the better the chances are that we will be happy with the results.

articleTitle: Rx for obsolescence: Shakespeare, Sophocles, and the Renaissance engineer — All are part of a plea for speaking out for technology
abstract: If ever innovation and enterprise were required, they are in these days of shrinking energy supplies, critical food and water shortages, failing transportation systems, urban decay, and social upheaval. In the solution of all these problems, the engineer has a role to play, but engineers may not be equal to the task. They may already be obsolescent — not technically inadequate, but socially inadequate.

articleTitle: Surviving the employment hot seat: Investigate a future employer thoroughly — before the interview
abstract: Picture this. A student nears the end of a successful job interview. Then the interviewer asks, “What do you know about the XYZ Corp.?” Or, “Why do you want to work for us?” At that point, the interviewee coughs nervously and mumbles something about the merits of XYZ's D/A converters. End of interview, end of employment possibility with XYZ, which manufactures display terminals.

articleTitle: Resume preparation and communication Part I: The impedance match: Both job seeker and employer are transmitter-receivers, but it's up to you to maximize the signal and reduce the noise
abstract: One of the most important career steps an engineer can take is the preparation of a complete and effective resume. When it is used in the search for a job, the resume must be viewed as a communication tool. That is, it must satisfy the needs of employment managers and engineering managers who see hundreds of resumes a month.

articleTitle: Computer communication networks: A case history: One computer network connects seven separate computers and allows users to access and share each other's resources
abstract: Computer networks consist of an interconnected collection of processors (hosts), network nodes (switches, communications switching computers) that connect the processors, and the communication links (transmission lines) [see Fig. 1]. They are used in electronic mail; inventory control; reservation systems; military command, control, and communication (C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>); office automation; and teleconferencing, among other applications. The goals of computer networks are to make it possible to share resources such as data bases, programs, and processors regardless of the physical location of the user and the resources; to provide the network user with the capability to communicate with other users; to provide reliable and alternative resources; to allow more than one processor to work on a particular problem (distribution); and to provide compatibility of dissimilar equipment and software.

articleTitle: Surviving the plant visit: Your plant visit need not be a comedy of errors. With preparation, you can turn a nerve-racking ordeal into an invitation to return — Permanently
abstract: I'll never forget that interview trip. About the only thing I did right was to fly in the day before. … First, I decided to wear my interview clothes because I was afraid the airline would lose my luggage. Well, it was pouring rain when we landed, and I got completely drenched. Then, I had trouble renting a car because I was under 25 and didn't have a major credit card with me. By the time I got to the motel, I was so tired I didn't read any of the company literature. To make matters worse, the next morning I got stopped for speeding in my rush to get to the interview on time. I finally made it through the day, but if ever I had to do it again …

articleTitle: EE at work: Corporate life at Ma Bell: The clout of working with top people and top equipment offsets the frustration of end results not quickly seen
abstract: Life in the big corporation. Byron Johns, age 26, has known it for almost four years, with one year away getting his Master's degree.

articleTitle: How to beat the job odds: Learn how to read between the lines, and you'll have a better idea of the kind of experience employers today are looking for
abstract: On any Sunday, in the Business or Financial Sections of any major newspaper, there appear want ads for an ever-increasing variety of engineering jobs. It seems as though industry has just discovered that without engineers, there can be no advances in technology, and therefore, in life-style, energy, and so on; in short, there can be no better mousetrap. At a time when the unemployment rate is at a historical high, and there is much debate about the engineering professions, a cursory look at these ads is most instructive. The trick is to know how to read them, i.e., how to interpret them, and how to use them to prepare for that fateful day when you are the one pounding the pavement.

articleTitle: View from the top: Semiconductors and the second industrial revolution: The first was essentially an oil-based revolution, while today's information revolution uses the fundamental technology of semiconductors
abstract: I am pleased to have this opportunity to communicate with EE students and to give you a brief history and update of the semiconductor industry. There are six major factors that comprise this business: markets, technology, international business, finance, people, and manufacturing. Here, I would like to capture for you some of the excitement of my vision for the future.

articleTitle: Join the writers' elite — If you can: Want to join the writers' elite? It's back to basics with reading, writing, and review
abstract: Of two equally competent professional engineers, the one who can write well has an unbeatable advantage. If he publishes two or three papers on a relatively narrow subject, he gets national recognition as an expert, and his silent colleague does not, even if he knows just as much about the subject. In fact, the writer is bound to get preferential treatment from his immediate superiors, even though they are aware that the other engineer is just as capable in every other respect.

articleTitle: A new photographic development from Kodak: Kodak's new decision-free disc camera is a product of many tough decisions and a synergistic management approach
abstract: At the touch of a button — and by means of two integrated electronic circuits — Kodak's latest contribution to the world of amateur photography analyzes the scene, sets the proper exposure, activates the built-in flash, takes the picture, advances the film, and recharges the flash — all in a split second's time. Known as the Kodak disc camera, the new system is considered the biggest innovation in amateur photography since the introduction of easy-load Kodak Instamatic cameras 19 years ago.

articleTitle: Graduate school or work? Some elementary truths about graduate degrees, as viewed by an EE department chairman
abstract: Graduate school, industry, or both? These are key questions facing graduating seniors in engineering. The world of work is extremely attractive: salary offers are high and besides, going to school may be getting old hat. But there are reasons to consider postponing work opportunities to go to graduate school full time.

articleTitle: All of the above … and more: Design considerations not taught in the classrooms
abstract: Today, a designer of electronics software and hardware must be aware that a commercial product should meet all required specifications, operate correctly, and be relatively easy to service when it fails to operate.

articleTitle: Insurance protection: Assessing your needs: Insurance programs abound, and as a student or recent graduate, you are a susceptible consumer. Being informed is the best policy
abstract: Real financial security is difficult to achieve without adequate insurance coverage. Yet, with the many types of insurance and different plans offered, it is often difficult to know what to buy. Because of the vast scope of the subject, we will discuss only three basic types of insurance coverage here — disability income, life, and health — the types that are most important to students and recent graduates. Other forms of insurance protection, such as property/casualty, may be subjects for another article.

articleTitle: View from the top: Career choice with responsibility: Engineers must remain tuned in to society and operate within a total system, from development to operations
abstract: We live in a highly, technological world, with media constantly informing us of the central importance of technology, citing the advances and needs in everything from manufacturing to national defense. In short, technological development is perceived as the key to many of society's needs.

articleTitle: Behind the scenes with the company recruiter: Long before you start looking for your first job, company recruiters are busy at work, preparing to ensure a good match between candidate and company
abstract: Most seniors begin looking for employment about nine months to one year before graduation. The first step is to register with the placement office on your campus where you are instructed on the proper procedures, i.e., how to use the placement library; how to sign up for an interview; how to use a resume to maximum advantage. This is followed by research on companies in which you are interested as well as selection of specific companies with which to interview. The placement office will then give you a sign-up sheet, which has the date and time of your interview with XYZ company.

articleTitle: Programming successful branch meetings: The secret ingredients for success are advance planning, people agreement, and good publicity
abstract: Whether it's getting a student paper contest, a speaker, or merely a beer blast off the ground, it takes work, coordination, and team effort to be successful. If your Student Branch's activities never go far or very well, here are some general suggestions on how to program successful Branch activities.

articleTitle: Fellow students from distant shores: The presence of foreign students is of social and economic significance. It is to our benefit to provide for them a welcome environment
abstract: In 1960, foreign students made up 1.5 percent of the college student population in the United States. By 1980, that figure had jumped to 2.6 percent, an estimated 311 880 of total college enrollment. At the present rate of growth, foreign student enrollment could reach 1 million, or 10 percent of all students, by the 1990s. It is interesting to note that in 1980, 25.8 percent of foreign students were enrolled in engineering fields and another 6.1 percent were in mathematics and computer science fields. There is every reason to believe that these percentages will continue to increase.

articleTitle: EE at work: Discovering the small company: Mark Davis' first job seemed like a faltering step, but redirection led him to surprising discoveries about himself and his job preferences
abstract: Mark Davis, at 22, was not really sure what he wanted to do when he graduated with a BSEE from the University of Utah in December 1980. He needed a job close by since his wife, Amy, was not graduating until May, and he knew he wanted a job that would give him experience supervising people. A job offer by U.S. Steel seemed to fit these criteria, but ultimately was not satisfying. Later in a small family business, which allowed him to be innovative and creative, Mark made some surprising discoveries about his job likes and dislikes and came full circle.

articleTitle: Questions that boost your Interview Quotient: The job interview: Will they choose you? Will you select them? The answer is in the questions
abstract: As an engineering student, you will have the opportunity to choose from many job offers which can take you to many career paths. Which position to accept is an important and perplexing decision, especially since, as an entry-level engineer, you might not know which tasks give you the greatest satisfaction and what the day-to-day life in a particular company is really like.

articleTitle: Resume preparation and communication Part II: The transmission effect: Once you have ensured a good impedance match (Part I), your message must be intelligently and effectively transmitted via the carrier
abstract: In Part I, which appeared in the Spring 1982 issue of IEEE Potentials, I showed you how to compile a resume biased toward a specific job, i.e., how to ensure a good impedance match. As in Part I, I will again use the electronics analogy to show you the most effective transmission to the right people, those in a position to offer you a job — either an existing one, or, if you're lucky, one “made” for you.

articleTitle: How to get to work: Trade in your passive study techniques, including the yellow Magic Marker
abstract: “I really studied for this test, and I thought I knew the material. Of course, I reviewed it the night before class, then I studied each chapter as we reviewed it in class. What's more, I used a yellow underliner, but …”

articleTitle: A professionally complete education: Identity crisis? IEEE student membership aids self-discovery
abstract: The Cheshire Cat in Alice in Wonderland provided that profound advice to Alice when she asked directions at a yet unchosen fork in the road. But it's hardly fairytale advice; all of us need specific goals if our decisions are going to be consistently valid in guiding our futures.

articleTitle: What is this IEEE business? The IEEE can be more than a resume filler. Your Student Branch activities can make you a more skilled student and place you in a favorable light
abstract: When I was an undergraduate at the University of Missouri (Columbia campus), nearly 20 years ago, I recall being strongly persuaded by a certain faculty member to attend student IEEE meetings and presentations. His tactics were rather effective since he took roll at these meetings. If a sizable number of students in his class were absent, he would pop quizzes the next day. Needless to say, attendance flourished, as he managed to move some of us through the “What's this IEEE?” fog.

After earning B.S.E.E. and M.S.E.E. degrees from Colorado State University, he joined Ralston as a construction engineer. Only four months later he was promoted to project engineer in the corporate engineering department. Steve is married and has two sons.

articleTitle: IEEE students set the PACE: This professional awareness conference resulted in heightened interest in the IEEE and a boost in membership
abstract: Engineering is more than a job, it is a profession. A professional must be technically competent, but he also has the responsibility of maintaining the integrity of his profession. There will be many ethical, social, and economic questions that we will have to deal with in the future. It is time that we as students learn how to handle these questions effectively, as we prepare ourselves for a professional career. It is the aim of this conference to complement our technical training by making us more aware of the concept and scope of professional practice.

We also hope to acquaint you with the IEEE, its inner workings, its goals, its resources, and its responses to situations of concern to its members.

articleTitle: Reading up books: The fascinating world of computer graphics: Computer graphics is rapidly becoming pervasive. Whether you are a potential developer or user, these publications will spur your involvement
abstract: Computer graphics, that is, producing a “picture” or “drawing” of some sort with a computer, is hardly a new field.

articleTitle: Books — Digital signal processing: First, an overview; then a survey of the basic texts
abstract: The field of digital signal processing originated in the 1960s and accelerated in growth in the 1970s. It includes several basic operations on signals: reconstruction of signals from samples, analysis of the characteristics of signals, and signal filtering. Signal reconstruction refers to the operation of reforming a continuously varying signal, such as a voltage, a speed measurement, and other factors, from a set of evenly spaced samples of the signal.

articleTitle: Reading up books: Integrated circuit engineering: A description of this relatively new area of electrical engineering is followed by a review of a few textbooks and journals
abstract: Since their invention in 1958, integrated circuits (ICs) have found their way into numerous electrical products. Their widespread use is due to the fact that they are extremely small, highly reliable, and attractively inexpensive. As a result, there is a growing demand for IC engineers, i.e. experts in their design and fabrication. There is an even larger demand for EEs who understand at least the basic fundamentals of this process, since this helps in making decisions about the selection and application of ICs.
